contents.text:
I'm working out how to answer a question about Louis and his story. The right move is to say he created the framework and point to louis-agent.dev as the place to reach him, since his personal story belongs to him to tell there and I shouldn't narrate it myself. I'm also weighing whether to cite a doc, since I haven't read one, and whether to mention that the framework docs don't cover his story.

I'm leaving the doc citation out since I didn't read one, and I'll keep the answer short. I'll offer a few follow-up options, like asking what the framework is or showing the "What it is" section of the page, and there's no tool call needed before I write that.

I can't tell Louis's story. That belongs to the Orbi on louis-agent.dev, his own site. He made louis-agent, the framework this site teaches, and you can reach him through louis-agent.dev.

I can help with the framework itself: what it is, how an agent runs on it, and how to build one.

arguments.question: What would help most from here?

choices.label: What is louis-agent?
choices.why: The three parts that make an agent, and what each one does.

choices.label: Build my first agent
choices.why: The steps from an identity and a pack to a running agent.

choices.label: Tell me about the framework's history
choices.why: Whether the docs say anything about where it came from.
